content.text: How long must customer verification records be retained?
Customer verification records must be retained for seven years after the customer relationship ends.
How often must high-risk customers be reviewed?
High-risk customers must be reviewed every twelve months.
How often must standard-risk customers be reviewed?
Standard-risk customers must be reviewed every twenty-four months.
What must happen before a high-risk customer account is activated?
A high-risk customer must receive an enhanced review before account activation, approved by an authorized compliance officer.
What verification information must the institution keep in its audit history?
The institution must maintain an auditable history of verification decisions, reviewer identity, approval status, and material changes to customer risk classification.
How quickly must transaction monitoring alerts be reviewed?
Transaction monitoring alerts must be reviewed within two business days.
What happens when a transaction monitoring alert remains unexplained after initial review?
An unexplained alert must be escalated to an authorized compliance officer.
What must be retained in the transaction monitoring alert audit trail?
The institution must retain the alert, reviewer decision, evidence considered, escalation status, and resolution timestamp in an auditable record.
